status: post hoc. Written after every study's results were known. It does not replace any study's frozen scoring rules; those remain each study's protocol outcome.
purpose: Score the six studies' existing estimates with one rule so their outcomes can be compared. No estimate is refitted.

scope.rescored: Coefficient-level targets with a published value and a reconstructed value.
scope.not_rescored: Fit and invariance diagnostics, F tests, text-only robustness statements and other targets without a published coefficient. Their study-rule outcomes stand.

magnitude.statistic: Distance from the reconstructed estimate to the published rounding interval, divided by the published SE (upper rounding bound). Taken from each study's scoring output.
magnitude.no_published_se: Use an SE derived from printed quantities when the study derived one (Twenge). Otherwise magnitude is not audited and the term is decided by sign and inference (Holderness).

sign.applies_when: The published estimate is significant at p < .10.
sign.mismatch: Opposite sign and the reconstructed estimate has p < .10.
sign.grey: Opposite sign and the reconstructed estimate has p >= .10.

inference.p_value: Native (model-based) p of the reconstructed estimate.
inference.published_band: From the paper's star legend as transcribed by each study, or from the upper rounding bound of a printed p value. When the legend allows two bands, use the weaker.
inference.one_tailed_papers: Delaney and Huselid (1996) print one-tailed stars. Both the published and the rebuilt bands are then one-tailed in the hypothesized direction, as computed by the study.
inference.mismatch: Reconstructed band two or more steps weaker than published.
inference.not_a_failure: Equal or stronger significance, including a reconstruction that becomes significant where the paper reports nonsignificance.

sample_size.rule: Above 0.15, every term of that model is indeterminate (sample not rebuilt). At or below 0.15 the N gap is reported only.

term_rules.inconsistent_targets: If the paper prints contradictory values for a target (for example table against text), the term is indeterminate.
term_rules.missing_estimate: A term an implementation failed to estimate is indeterminate.
term_rules.term_outcome: Any mismatch: candidate. Otherwise any grey: indeterminate. Otherwise: consistent.
term_rules.reader_origins: When the readers' interpretations produced more than one origin specification, the term outcome must be the same at every origin; otherwise it is indeterminate (label-sensitive).

discrepancy: A candidate becomes discrepant only after an adversarial review by a model family independent of every implementer and a human confirmation. No study has such a review, so every candidate is unverified and formally indeterminate.
claim_rule: Consistent if every focal term of the claim is consistent. Candidate if any focal term is a candidate. Otherwise indeterminate.

paper_rule.consistent: Every focal claim consistent and no lower-tier candidate.
paper_rule.partially_reproduced: Every focal claim consistent and at least one lower-tier candidate.
paper_rule.not_reproduced_unverified: At least one focal claim is a candidate. Formally indeterminate until a candidate is verified.

focal_structure: Each study's focal claims and their terms, as fixed by its readers before results. The mapping is listed in score_common.py.

sensitivity_variant.name: lenient
sensitivity_variant.changes: Magnitude bands 2.0 and 4.0. An N gap above 0.15 blocks a candidate (it becomes indeterminate) but not a consistent outcome.
